description: Read direct holdings or pooled fund look-through positions across the connected investor's imported accounts. Use for what the investor owns and shared direct/indirect exposure. These are alternative views of the same capital, never additive. Preserve the snapshot base currency, pricing and constituent dates, unknown mass, coverage and denominators. Returns a bounded page; send computed_at on further pages and restart if the snapshot changes. Requires explicit portfolio:read consent and portfolio-detail entitlement. Missing snapshots return unavailable; no analytics are fabricated.
name: get_portfolio_holdings

dissolved.description: How the funds this counter counts resolved: fully dissolved, partly dissolved, or not at all. Funds that can be looked through, which means funds that can hold stocks. A bond, cash (money market, overnight), gold or crypto fund is never counted here: it cannot hold a listed company, so it is never dissolved and is reported instead as an opaque sleeve, held as a whole, in its own asset class. An equity fund whose constituent fetch failed IS counted, under `none`: it is a fund that can be looked through and has not been, which is a gap rather than a rule.

etfCount.description: Funds that can be looked through, which means funds that can hold stocks. A bond, cash (money market, overnight), gold or crypto fund is never counted here: it cannot hold a listed company, so it is never dissolved and is reported instead as an opaque sleeve, held as a whole, in its own asset class. A fund is an ISIN, not a holding row: one ETF held at two brokers counts once, and the overlap pairs are drawn from this same population.

reason.description: Serve-time localized text. The engine stores its reason key here; the serve layer replaces it with text in the caller's language.

reasonKey.description: Language-free reason key. Absent on a payload cached before keys existed, whose `reason` then passes through as the German text the engine wrote (for example `Als Ganzes gehalten`), whatever the caller's language, until that payload is recomputed. `pending` covers two situations a caller may want to tell apart and today cannot: the constituent fetch failed on this run, and the provider returns no constituents for this wrapper at all, which no retry will change.

fetchedAt.description: When the oldest price behind this answer was fetched (ISO 8601 UTC). On an aggregate the oldest row wins, so the whole answer is dated by its stalest figure. Null exactly when no price behind this answer carries a fetch timestamp: an empty book, a book whose every row is unvalued, or a book priced only by figures the user entered. The null arm is not an error state, and `fetchedAt !== null` is the one predicate that is true exactly when a real fetch stands behind these numbers.

provenance.description: The provider that supplied the price, and when it did. A provenance is the provider AND the moment, or nothing, so this is null on every answer whose `fetchedAt` is null, and also on a dated answer whose provider is not recorded: the X-Ray surfaces read a two-value price-source column that cannot separate the scheduled batch from the realtime feed, so they date the envelope and decline to attribute it.

source.description: How the price reached us: `live` from the realtime feed, `batch` from the scheduled refresh, `manual` from a value the user entered, and `none` exactly when no row behind this answer carries a price. On an aggregate the most degraded row source wins. Do not read a source other than `none` as evidence of a fetch: a manual-only book reports `manual`, which is a figure the user typed rather than one anybody fetched.

stalenessMs.description: Age of `fetchedAt` in milliseconds, as the server measured it for this answer. Use it instead of comparing `fetchedAt` against the device clock, which can be wrong. The X-Ray serve surfaces re-derive it on every request, so a stale-while-revalidate answer ages honestly. Null exactly when `fetchedAt` is null. Guard the comparison rather than trusting the arm: `null < n` is true in JavaScript, so read `stalenessMs !== null && stalenessMs < n`, or the null arm reads as freshly fetched.

title: Read portfolio holdings
